QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_27

question.text: A 95% confidence interval on an outcome proportion means:

answer.text: There is a 95% probability the true population proportion lies within the computed interval
If we repeated the sampling procedure many times, approximately 95% of the computed intervals would contain the true population proportion
95% of the sampled individuals reported the outcome
The outcome is statistically significant at the 5% level

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The technically correct interpretation of a 95% CI is frequentist: if the sampling procedure is repeated many times and a CI is computed each time, ~95% of those intervals will contain the true parameter. Option A is the common Bayesian-style misstatement. **The Trap:** Option A is the most common intuitive but technically loose interpretation. Option C confuses CI with point-estimate. Option D confuses CI with significance test. **Cross-Exam Context:** XV Research Analyst, X-A IA, and research-methods syllabi test this distinction frequently. XXIII demands frequentist-correct language in the SIR. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** In your SIR, never write 'there is a 95% probability the true value lies in [a,b]' — use 'we are 95% confident…' or the frequentist phrasing. It's a small thing but statistician-reviewers of your AIR notice.
